nodes.label: Ethics and regulation
nodes.question: What is the primary focus of the paragraph regarding financial institutions in the context of energy transition?
nodes.answer: The primary focus is on the role of public bilateral financial institutions, particularly Export Credit Agencies (ECAs), in redirecting financial flows from fossil fuels to renewable energy.
nodes.paragraph: Abstract Achieving a clean energy transition requires global financial flows to be redirected away from fossil fuels and into renewable energy. While capital market actors and multilateral financial institutions have been the subject of significant scholarly attention, public bilat - eral financial institutions, especially Export Credit Agencies (ECAs), have been largely overlooked. This is an important oversight given ECAs are the source of billions of dollars of public finance for fossil fuels, which has helped to lock-in recipient countries to fossil fuel energy systems. Using a panel dataset of ECA transactions in the energy sector, we show that despite some improvements in financial flows after the Paris Agreement in 2015, fossil fuel investments remain pervasive and growth in clean energy investments is mini - mal. To better understand changes in ECA portfolios, we examine the cases of the Export- Import Bank of the United States (Exlm) and UK Export Finance (UKEF). Drawing on elite interviews, we identify three factors that are shaping Exlm S and UKEF S capacity to promote renewable energy exports: the extent of political control over the bureaucracy, the size and composition of green industrial bases, and the policy tools available to both ECAs to support the renewables sector.

nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How do Exlm and UKEF differ in their responsiveness to governmental pressure regarding fossil fuel lending?
nodes.answer: Exlm has statutory autonomy, allowing it to resist executive orders, while UKEF responds directly to executive pressure by transitioning its lending portfolio.
nodes.paragraph: To better understand changes in ECA portfolios at the organizational level, we conduct two in-depth case studies of ECAs. To do so, we draw on elite interviews with Exlm and UKEF. Despite their mandates to promote national exports including fossil fuels, both ECAs are now governed by a suite of climate change policies and have made commitments to green their portfolios, with varying levels of success. We identify three key factors that affect the capacity of Exlm and UKEF to promote renewable exports. First, is the extent of political control of the bureaucracy, which directly affects how responsive ECAs are to pressure from the executive and legislatures to transi - tion their lending portfolios towards renewable energy. In the US, Exlm S statutory auton - omy has resulted in the bank resisting executive orders to limit fossil fuel lending. Whereas UKEF, which as a government department does not have statutory autonomy, has directly responded to executive pressure by transitioning its lending portfolio. Second is the size of the state S green industrial base. In countries with mature renewable energy industries, which have satisfied domestic demand, there will be more demand for export credits.

nodes.label: Ethics and regulation
nodes.question: What was the main goal of the Export Finance for Future (E3F) coalition launched in 2021?
nodes.answer: The main goal of the E3F coalition was to align export finance with international climate objectives.
nodes.paragraph: For example, in 2015 OECD countries agreed to restrict export finance for coal-fired power projects (Liao 2021 ). In 2021 European countries launched the Export Finance for Future (E3F) coalition to specifically align export finance with international climate objectives (E3F 2023 ). In the same year, 34 countries signed the Glasgow Statement, which commits signatories to ending public financial support for international fossil fuel projects (DuFour et al. 2022 ). At the national level, many G20 governments have responded by implementing new climate targets. For example, in 2022 European ECAs committed to ending export credit for fossil fuel energy projects (IISD 2022 ), and several other ECAs, including the Export-Import Bank of the US (Exlm) and the UK Export Finance (UKEF) have announced policies to limit public finance for fossil fuels (DuFour et al. 2022 ). While the pressure on ECAs is likely to increase, we do not have a good understanding of the potential for these public bilateral financial institutions to accelerate a clean energy transition. To the extent that ECAs have been studied, the initial focus has been on tracking financial flows from specific countries, such as China, or focussing on particular fuels, such as coal (Chen et al.

nodes.question: What are the seven major themes of sustainable finance research identified in the study?
nodes.answer: The seven major themes are socially responsible investing, climate financing, green financing, impact investing, carbon financing, energy financing, and governance of sustainable financing and investing.
nodes.paragraph: Abstract Sustainable nance is a rich eld of research. Yet, existing reviews remain limited due to the piecemeal insights offered through a sub-set rather than the entire corpus of sustainable nance. To address this gap, this study aims to conduct a large-scale review that would pro- vide a state-of-the-art overview of the performance and intellectual structure of sustainable nance. To do so, this study engages in a review of sustainable nance research using big data analytics through machine learning of scholarly research. In doing so, this study unpacks the most in uential articles and top contributing journals, authors, institutions, and countries, as well as the methodological choices and research contexts for sustainable nance research. In addition, this study reveals insights into seven major themes of sustainable nance research, namely socially responsible investing, climate nancing, green nancing, impact investing, carbon nancing, energy nancing, and governance of sustainable nancing and investing. To drive the eld forward, this study proposes several suggestions for future sustainable nance research, which include developing and diffusing innovative sustainable nancing instruments, magnifying and managing the pro tability and returns of sustainable nancing, making sustainable nance more sustainable, devising and unifying policies and frameworks for sustainable nance, tackling greenwashing of corporate sustainability reporting in sus- tainable nance, shining behavioral nance on sustainable nance, and leveraging the power of new-age technologies such as arti cial intelligence, blockchain, internet of things, and machine learning for sustainable nance.

nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: What is the significance of the broad nature of sustainable finance as discussed in the paragraph?
nodes.answer: The broad nature of sustainable finance is significant for achieving the sustainability agenda and has prompted many studies to enhance understanding and practice in this area.
nodes.paragraph: This calls for a broader and more encompassing de nition that speaks to sustain- ability at large. In this regard, we propose that sustainable nance should encompass all activities and factors that would make nance sustainable and contribute to sustainability , a de nition that we opine complements the myriad goals by different stakeholders, such as the European Commission S ESG and the United Nations SDGs. Indeed, the attainment of sustainable policy objectives across numerous jurisdictions can be achieved through various ways such as climate nance, carbon and ESG disclosure, green bonds, and socially respon- sible investment (Alsai et al., 2020 ; Barua & Chiesa, 2019 ; Lokuwaduge & Heenetigala, 2017 ; Migliorelli, 2021 E C D , 2020 Widyawati, 2020 ), all of which can be covered under our umbrella de nition of sustainable nance. Considering the broad nature of sustainable nance and its importance for achieving the sustainability agenda, many studies have been undertaken to enhance the understanding and practice of sustainable nance. The recent review of sustainable nance by Cunha et al. ( 2021 ) exempli es this observation, as the authors found that the extant literature on sustainable nance to be excessively fragmented , which makes it dif cult to identify what constitutes the eld and what differentiates it from traditional nance .

nodes.question: What is the main objective of the current study on sustainable finance?
nodes.answer: The main objective is to provide a state-of-the-art overview of sustainable finance research by considering all aspects and related articles in the field, encompassing a broader scope than previous reviews.
nodes.paragraph: However, their review, which shed light on the critical features of sustainable nance, the global initiatives for the promotion of sustainable nance, and the strategies and outcomes of the main players in sustainable nance, considered 166 articles only, though the eld is in fact very much larger, as we demonstrate through the present review consisting of 936 articles. Noteworthily, no review, to date, has attempted to analyze the burgeoning eld of sustainable nance without making excessive concessions, wherein overly stringent criteria are imposed to trim the corpus for review to a manageable size for review, as witness in the review by Cunha et al. ( 2021 ). In this study, we aim to provide a state-of-the-art overview of sustainable nance research, taking into account all aspects and related articles in the eld. That is to say, this study covers 123Annals of Operations Research (2025) 345:1061 1104 1062 the entire spectrum of sustainable nance, and thus, it is not limited to any single aspect of the concept, as in the case of past reviews such as climate nance (Giglio et al., 2020 ) and green nance (Malhotra & Thakur, 2020 ).
